previous_authorization.note: This is the second continuation authorization of this run. It does not supersede or reopen the previous window.

cp01.reason: Three SECURITY DEFINER functions hard-code the root5 generation id; two also hard-code the superseded window literal and the binding-forward cap. The run cannot proceed on root5 because the root5 GENERATION_REGISTERED event (clued_control.events sequence 5) declares expires_at 2026-09-11T10:21:05Z and the controller runs currentWindow over that body.

required_transaction_form.lock: access exclusive on the eight clued_control tables

prior_unreviewed_change_disclosure.what: reserve_gate and reserve_execution_budget were rewritten outside this repository on 2026-09-11 as part of the previous window migration.
prior_unreviewed_change_disclosure.receipt_wording: This rewrite has no corresponding pull request or published evidence in this repository.
prior_unreviewed_change_disclosure.consequence: That migration missed append_status_manifest, which still pins the superseded window 2026-09-11T10:21:05Z while another check in the same function requires expires_at to be later than now. Status24 has been unappendable since that moment.

sixth_edit_class_added_after_round_10.why_it_is_needed: reserve_gate:35 and reserve_execution_budget:40 pin sha256 of the whole read_execution()->'root' to 4ddd23b5... The actual value is e7624fda..., so BOTH FUNCTIONS ALREADY FAIL TODAY, independently of root6. Cause: root carries metadata_binding_sha256, the digest of the whole accepted_binding row, and the unreviewed 2026-09-11 out-of-band window migration changed that row without updating this guard. It went unnoticed because neither function has been successfully called since 2026-09-11 03:47:18Z. The guard belongs to none of the five classes above, so it needs this one.
sixth_edit_class_added_after_round_10.shape_granted: Replace the single failing assertion with three, all computable before any write: (i) sha256 over the five frozen historical root events, byte for byte INCLUDING recorded_at, pinned to 45c6a2cbaf33bb27f6b4c136440d71d767943acfa9772867e219627759ca5bbc; (ii) sha256 over every other root key plus the registration event with only recorded_at removed, pinned to a value derived before the CP-01 transaction and published for review; (iii) jsonb_array_length(root->'events') is exactly 6.
sixth_edit_class_added_after_round_10.expected_values_must_be_computed_in_data: jsonb key order is Postgres's, not insertion order and not lexicographic. This is the R9-F1 lesson applied to a second place.

carve_out_from_prohibited.what_is_being_narrowed: one check's digest domain, by exactly one field: recorded_at of the registration event
carve_out_from_prohibited.why_that_field_costs_no_strength: It is written by clock_timestamp(), so no caller can set it; append_event independently pins clock_timestamp() inside [not_before, expires_at); and the events_immutable trigger forbids UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE afterwards. Its immutability is enforced elsewhere, so removing it from this digest removes redundancy, not coverage.

options_considered_and_refused.(a) digest over root excluding events: refused: abandons all event coverage with no compensation
options_considered_and_refused.(d) assert structured fields instead of: refused: abandons metadata_binding_sha256 and events coverage; the only genuinely weakening option
options_considered_and_refused.(c) leave the guard in CP-01 untouched a: refused: the implementer preferred it, the independent reviewer rejected it. It needs a second SECURITY DEFINER replacement INSIDE the runbook's irreversible zone, where there is no rollback, no refund and no permitted blind retry; it conflicts with cp01.required_transaction_form.single_transaction; and its expected value would be read back by the reviewed party from state it had just written, replacing an in-advance auditable constant with an after-the-fact self-read. See SuccessorReviewerRound10.md sections 6 and 8.
options_considered_and_refused.(b) strip recorded_at from every event: acceptable but superseded by (e), which keeps the five historical recorded_at values

repository_side.note: Authorised here alongside the database side. Previously the only authorisation for this half was OwnerForwardCapExtensionOverride.json, which this clause supersedes.

supersedes.why: That record was never independently reviewed and its stated reason rested on a premise later shown false. It is superseded rather than amended, and the independent opinion required for this clause is ForwardCapExtensionIndependentOpinion20260912.json.

forward_cap_extension.why_needed: Moving the execution binding onto the rebuilt controller requires a twentieth binding forward; the fifteenth counted forward was consumed on 2026-09-11.

prior_record_caveat.false_premise: The implementing side told the Owner the cap merely lacked a backing document. In fact the database enforced the cap in two functions and the raise was not executable at all.

rejected_alternative.what: Rewrite effective_execution_binding() directly so no forward is needed and the cap stays at 15.
rejected_alternative.rejected_because: It would move the execution binding silently, outside the append-only event log.

generation_registration.why: Until cp01 is applied the control plane requires the live generation to be root5. Registering first would break the existing path without opening the new one, and append_event's generation_reuse_or_rollback forbids re-registering root5.

controller_rebuild.reason: root6Expiry was set to 2026-09-19T00:00:00Z when the root6 controller was built, and expiryForBudget(sequence >= 89) requires a new budget to declare exactly that value. reserve_execution_budget additionally requires a new budget's expires_at to be no later than accepted_binding.expires_at. Under the fixed 86400-second window rule that value can never be produced.

not_affected.why: It pins the root6 generation only, and the generation does not change.

estimate_correction.what_was_missed: All four capacity documents pin the window 2026-09-19T00:00:00Z or the controller digest 72d9eb92, not only capacity_delta.

recorded_governance_question.question: The controller under qualification is built by the implementing side. Under this approval the enforcement layer it must satisfy is also modified by the implementing side, specifically so that this controller passes. What does the resulting qualification result certify?
recorded_governance_question.context: Seven rounds of independent review examined the repository side only. The database side was not reviewed by anyone until immediately before the single irreversible write, and a prior unreviewed change to these same functions is what left append_status_manifest inconsistent.
recorded_governance_question.required_in_final_result: The final qualification result must state plainly that the enforcement layer of this qualification run was modified by the party being qualified, before the run.

referenced_documents.why_this_section_exists: Two documents this approval relies on live only on the independent reviewer's branch and are not on main; merging this pull request does not bring them in. Rather than leave dangling repository-relative paths in a signed artifact, each is pinned to an immutable commit and to its own sha256, so the Owner and any later auditor can fetch exactly the bytes this approval was granted against. A third reference cited the wrong directory and is corrected above.
